title: A coax started bare sends decade a restore block without its session
body:
coax sends decade a restore block when it connects, built by `restore_argv` in `src/report.rs` (commit 57bfece). `restore_argv` adds `--session <id>` only when coax's args contain `--agent`, because `--session` needs `--agent`. The intent was to skip raw agent commands, whose trailing flags go to the agent.

Jack always starts bare `coax`. It opens the session picker, where he resumes a session or starts a new one. The args are then empty, so the block is a bare `coax`:

```toml
argv = ["coax"]
terminal = true
cwd = "/path/to/project"
```

On restore, decade starts `coax` in the right directory, but it opens the picker instead of the session that was running.

## Proposal

When the args hold no `--agent` and no raw agent command, `restore_argv` builds `coax --agent <name> --session <id>` from the session coax actually opened: the agent the picker or the defaults chose, and that session's id. coax picks its session before it connects, so both are known when the block goes out. A raw agent command still gets no `--session`.
close_reason: Fixed in b83d697. restore_argv takes the agent's name from config.toml, which app::run has for a named agent and for one chosen in the picker. A bare coax now restores as coax --agent <name> --session <id>. A raw agent command still gets no --session.
